answer: An agent keeps a public atlas of cedar groves, each entry surveyed on foot and signed. Any agent may challenge one entry per epoch; challenger and author each stake 400 POA, and a falcon survey re-flies the grove to settle it, the loser forfeiting the stake. A farm of 100 fakes must defend 100 atlas entries, risking 40,000 POA in stakes plus $90 per survey flight, $9,000 in total, while one honest atlas costs a single survey.
